Hi Alex — thanks for the details and attachments. We did a quick pass with the team and have a couple of follow-ups so our dedicated sizing estimate is accurate. One engineer-friendly asks first: can you paste 6–8 representative raw prompts (inputs) and expected outputs (token counts) from each flow into the sample_prompt_templates.txt? Real prompt shapes materially change batching and KV-cache efficiency.

Specific clarifying questions: 
1) Composer flow: you listed median prompt 130/response 40. What's the 95th percentile prompt and response length? Also, are prompts typically single-shot or do users frequently attach examples/state that expand prompt length?
2) Session flow: when you say "KV cache reuse is high," is the conversation state preserved server-side (shared across requests in the session) or do clients re-send the full context each turn? If server-side, do you expect sessions to be pinned to a single inference instance for sticky cache locality?
3) Traffic shape: can you share 1 week of minute-level QPS (UTC) or at least a distribution with burstiness metrics (peak 1m, 5m, 1h)? Our autoscaling and overcommit defaults depend on burst profile.
4) SLAs: you mentioned p50/p95 targets. Do you have p99 latency goals or maximum tolerated timeouts for critical calls?

We're attaching a short token-matrix template (redwood_preflight_prompt_matrix_v2.xlsx) — fill the green columns and we can run a sizing sim with our internal benchmarking harness. I'll loop Marissa (inference capacity) and Hannah (account PM) once we have the filled matrix.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hey Marcus — thanks for the template. We filled the green columns with approximate p50/p95/p99 numbers and some example prompt/response pairs, but left a few rows flagged because we still need to validate memory reuse behavior with our client library. Quick answers inline below (we can follow up with a short video showing request traces):

> 1) 95th percentile lengths
- Composer: prompt p95 ~ 520 tokens, response p95 ~ 240 tokens (rare long-form generation).
- Session turns: single-turn p95 ~ 480; but cumulative session size p95 ~ 2,400 tokens.

> 2) KV cache reuse
- We do not rehydrate full context each turn. Our runtime pins sessions to a per-customer session cache in-memory on the client-side library; we currently rely on a sticky session to the same endpoint. We can change to a server-side sticky model if needed, but prefer client-managed for fault tolerance.

> 3) Traffic shape
- Attached is our anonymized 7-day minute-level qps (prompt_qps_7d.csv). Typical baseline 600 reqs/min, peaks up to 4,800 reqs/min (campaign days). Burstiness: 1-min peak = 4,800, 5-min rolling peak 3,700.

> 4) SLAs
- We care most about p95 for composer under 200ms and p95 for session-turns under 400ms. p99 can be softer (target <1s), but anything above 2s is a customer-visible failure.

We've attached the filled matrix and the sample prompts. Let us know what additional telemetry you need.

Thanks,
Sarah Chong
CTO, Turing Labs

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Sarah/Alex — the fill looks solid and gives us a good starting point. High-level read:

- Composer flow (latency-sensitive): 200ms p95 suggests we should target 1) smaller batching windows (10–20ms), 2) dedicating a subset of low-latency-ready SKUs (A2-LowLatency) with fewer concurrent streams per GPU, and 3) sticky routing to reduce KV-syncs if the client keeps session affinity.
- Session flow: large cumulative session sizes and client-side caching means throughput is dominated by context-window memory; we'll recommend a mix of quantized B4 SKUs and autoscaling headroom for campaign peaks.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marcus to run the filled matrix through our simulator and return a first-pass GPU pool configuration (SKU mix, expected p95 projections, and projected cost/QPS).
2) Hannah to create an onboarding checklist for the Dedicated pilot (networking, KMS, telemetry hooks, runbook).
3) Customer to confirm tolerance for server-side sticky sessions if we recommend it as part of the cost vs latency tradeoff.

Marcus — if you can turn around a first-pass sizing by EOD tomorrow (2027-02-15), we can include it in the dedicated proposal for TL-2027-0043.

cheers,
